headline: Belmont Cragin's ward leads on polluted-site exposure, trails on new housing.
summary:
Belmont Cragin, Hermosa, Portage Park and Avondale make up Ward 31 on the Northwest Side. An overall score of 36.09 puts the ward 37th among the fifty, under the midpoint of the city. It holds the smallest measured exposure to polluted sites of the fifty wards, and 71.7 percent of its households speak a language other than English at home, the fourth highest share in Chicago. Aldermanic menu money here spreads across a wide run of blocks rather than bunching in one corner, city crews close street light outages in an average of 1.68 days, among the fastest turnarounds anywhere in the city, and about 26.7 percent of households have a householder living alone, ranking eighth of the fifty on that measure.

The weaker numbers cluster around housing and health coverage. An estimated 18.3 percent of residents have no health insurance, the highest uninsured share in the city. Parking disputes and complaints also run higher here than anywhere else in Chicago, across both measures the ward tracks, and builders pulled only one new residential permit last year, the fewest citywide. Rodent baiting requests take longer to close here than in any other ward. Ward 31 pairs clean industrial-site numbers and fast city response on basic requests with a housing supply that has nearly stopped growing.
reading_the_rankings:
Take the top ranking on polluted-site proximity. It looks like a clean sweep, but confidence is not high here, by the source's own grading, and a few wards never reported this measure at all, so the comparison sits on a thinner field than the full fifty.

Ward 31's last-place finish on new homes permitted looks like an outlier, but it barely is. Twenty-nine other wards sit less than two points off its score, and citywide, most wards land somewhere inside a five-point band on this measure, so the bottom of this list is really most of Chicago packed into one narrow stretch.

The menu-spending rankings carry a different asterisk. These lines are only a couple of years old, redrawn in 2023, so some of the historical spending behind the fifth-place mark on spending spread and the sixth-place mark on sidewalk spending was actually recorded against a differently shaped ward.

news.headline: Woman Killed At Busy NW Side Intersection Where Planned Traffic Light Was Never Installed
news.note: A 62-year-old woman was fatally struck by a driver in Hermosa at Belmont and Kilbourn, an intersection where a traffic signal has been planned since 2023.

news.headline: Ordinance Would Allow More Package Liquor Licenses On West Belmont Avenue
news.note: The ward's alderman co-sponsored a City Council ordinance amending the municipal code to allow additional package goods licenses on part of West Belmont Avenue.

alderperson.name: Felix Cardona Jr.
alderperson.verification_note: Fetched https://www.ward31.org/ directly this session. It is the official City of Chicago 31st Ward hub and names Felix Cardona as the ward's alderman. The wards.json data had no website on file for this ward, so this one was found and verified fresh.
